On a breach, stop and explain it in the report. If the fix needs `packages/objectql/**` or `packages/spec/**`, stop and report before writing.
Container & model: `M`, `mode:subagent`, `model: opus` (dispatch-gates --tier at 8145424b53: no path-derived mandate; default tier), `effort: xhigh` (an authz composition; the same family as #35914, which took four rounds)
Clause-②: yes (widening, expected; the dev confirms from the measured verdict and the claim is amended if it differs): a by-id update or delete by an owner-creator under an authored permissive widener is admitted on a row the platform floor alone admitted, where it is refused today.
Metadata-protocol: none
Responsibility: `plugin-security authz composition in objectstack (security-plugin-rls-filter.ts: the #5492 allow REMOVES isPlatformOwnershipFloorPolicy from the OR of permissive policies instead of replacing it with a true term) | none: no platform path admits the row once the floor is filtered out | owner-creators editing or deleting their own row by id on an object with an authored permissive update/delete policy; a loud 403, reachable today`
Thread-read: 7049054086
Premise: holds. At origin/main 8145424b53, `security-plugin-rls-filter.ts` :390-392 reads `const allRlsPolicies = opts?.dropPlatformOwnershipFloor ? collected.filter((p) => !isPlatformOwnershipFloorPolicy(p)) : collected;`, so with an authored permissive widener present the OR loses the floor term and gains nothing for it.
Serial constraints cleared: overlap-check probe over the four src files at origin/main 8145424b53: VERDICT clean, 0 open PR heads share them. #35914 (#35802 predicate half) merged 1c4db09ab and is on this base. #35934 touches the same files and waits behind this card in d7-C.
Pre-claim lane: `packages/plugins/**` (domain:server). area:data p2. Seat 7 order 2026-11-21T11:13Z (Tesla 11:10Z: data cards resume, at most 10 concurrent; no p1 data cards left, so p2s dispatch).
Pre-claim deps: no `Blocked-by:`. #5492 (the composition this corrects) is closed; #35802's controlled_by_parent half is open and waits on a maintainer card, and does not share this question.
Prior rulings read: allow,plugin-security,by-id,write,sharing,drops,owner_only_writes,permissive,policies,owner-creator,holding,authored (+2 more) → 196 hits; ADR-0055 Decision §3, ADR-0058 D3, ADR-0131 D13, ADR-0155 D1, ADR-0029 D9.7, ADR-0054 Decision §3, ADR-0055 Decision §4; thread: none; repo: objectstack-ai/objectstack. These stand: the #5492 composition (`allow` replaces the platform floor; `abstain`/`deny` keep it; app-authored policies, restrictive ones included, reach the compiler untouched); ADR-0066 ① (modifyAllRecords does not bypass write-side RLS on an ordinary posture). The fix changes how `allow` replaces the floor (a true term in place of a deleted one), not whether it does.
Owed review: CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER (Fable), because this changes what a by-id write can touch on an authz surface. L1 by L1-a. Run check-governed-merges before routing. If it is Tier H or turns out a narrowing, hand off to the seat for the four pieces.
Pins owed: the owner-creator on a closed row under the widener (by-id update and delete admitted), the Modify All holder under the widener (unchanged), a CONTROL restrictive authored policy that still refuses, and the by-id and predicate paths agreeing on the #35914 matrix with the widener case added. Ablate each.

repo:objectstack#7 · os-tesla · session_01L9qibzo28WC7HsvkY8hvV3

## Decision analysis · 2026-11-21T12:45Z

## 维护者速读

- 问题:对象上一旦配了"满足条件的记录可以修改或删除"这类规则(例如"进行中的商机谁都能改"),记录的创建人兼负责人逐条去改或删自己那条不满足条件的记录会被拒绝,而用批量修改却能改成功,同一件事两个答案;现有示例应用和 CRM 应用的这类规则都写成"全部记录放行",所以今天还没有客户撞上。
- 选项:A 放行,创建人照旧能逐条改、删自己建的记录,逐条和批量结果一致,1 个 PR(分支已做好);B 收紧,这类规则对创建人也生效,批量也跟着不再改这些记录,属于破坏性变更,1 个 PR 并且要先改后面那张批量性能卡的前提;C 新增一种"限制型规则",让"加权限"和"设上限"分开写,要先立设计决议再做,至少 3 个 PR。
- 推荐 A:规范、文档和教给 AI 的写法一直说"多条规则任一条允许就允许",真实应用也只把这类规则当"加权限"用,放行是让系统回到已经写明的含义。
- 不定会怎样:逐条被拒、批量成功的矛盾继续留着,而且"让成员对大量别人名下的记录做批量修改时变快"的那张卡依赖这个裁定,会一直被卡住不能开工。

## Analysis (English)

**One-sentence problem.** On an object that carries a rule such as "anyone may edit an open deal", the person who created and owns a closed deal is refused when they edit or delete it one record at a time, yet the same change goes through as a bulk update; the platform gives two answers to one question and no ruling says which one is meant.

### Background

- Until #6684 merged (2026-08-08T13:24Z), a member's update or delete was judged by the member baseline ("the rows you created", shipped as the `owner_only_writes` / `owner_only_deletes` policies on `member_default`) OR any app-authored policy, with record sharing as a separate AND. A row the caller created was always admitted by the baseline term.
- #5492, maintainer ruling recorded in comment 5219846435 (2026-08-07T16:59Z): "enforce both declared write-widening mechanisms" (Modify All, `edit` shares). #6684 implemented it by id: when record sharing answers `allow`, the baseline policy is removed from the policy set. Alone, nothing is left and the row is admitted, which is the widening that was ruled. Beside an authored policy, the authored policy is the only term left, so a row the caller created that the policy does not match went from admitted to refused. Nobody ruled that part; the comment at the site says app-authored policies "keep refusing exactly as before".
- #5493, maintainer ruling recorded in comment 5226389104 (2026-08-08T13:49Z): an app-authored update policy that matches a row lifts record sharing's refusal by id. This is the second ruling in the family, and it also reads an authored write policy as something that adds access.
- #24746 / PR #24792 (merged 2026-10-20T07:41Z) pinned ADR-0090 D10 (a delegated write never exceeds its delegator) with fixtures whose refused rows are rows the delegator created. The semantic question on that card was answered by the seat (comment 6285457301, 2026-10-20T07:10Z: "narrowing only"); the maintainer's word there (6285308967, 2026-10-20T07:00Z) set the release target and nothing else.
- #35802 / PR #35914 (merged 2026-11-21T03:34Z) made a bulk write take "the by-id decision for each matched row", except where an authored write policy applies to the caller: there it keeps the baseline term and asks no verdict, and its own test names the difference "the by-id corner, reported out of scope".
- #35917 was filed from that corner. The dev built option A at `0f31476970`; 22 pins of the #24746 family turn from refused to admitted, so the dev reported `needs_decision` (comment 7062563042, 2026-11-21T12:26Z).

### Governing text

- Spec, `packages/spec/src/security/rls.zod.ts`: "**Default Deny, among the policies that apply**: once a policy applies to the caller and the operation, a row that none of them admits is denied" (:122); "`update`: the existing rows an update may change, by id or `multi: true`" (:440); "by defining multiple policies (they OR-combine)" (:504). Line 109 states the OR for reads and points to `check` for writes. Search: `grep -n -E "OR-combine|Default Deny, among|by id or" packages/spec/src/security/rls.zod.ts`.
- ADR-0066, Precedence §3: "Multiple row policies for the same object/operation are OR-combined … (any matching policy admits the row …)"; §4: "Until then there is no implicit deny except the gates in (1) and fail-closed defaults"; ①: "`modifyAllRecords` bypasses write-side RLS for that object … but *only* when the object's posture permits it". Search: `grep -n -o -E "OR within an object|no implicit deny|bypasses write-side RLS" docs/adr/0066-unified-authorization-model.md` (lines 116, 117, 64).
- Docs, `content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx:119-121`, introduced there as "the contract, not an implementation detail": "Multiple row policies for the same object/operation OR-combine their `using` on reads and on the rows a write may target". Search: `grep -n "rows a write may target" content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx`.
- The #5492 ruling (5219846435) and the #5493 ruling (5226389104), both quoted above. Both rule a widening; neither says an authored policy takes a row away.
- `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/platform-ownership-policies.ts:33-35`: the gate "may only replace the floor the PLATFORM shipped — an app-authored policy is a declared security property and must always reach the compiler (ADR-0049)".
- ADR-0090 D10 rule 1, "Intersection, never union": the invariant the 22 pins serve. It says nothing about how the delegator's own write is composed.
- None found: a spec line or ADR decision saying an authored update or delete `using` policy takes away a row another applicable policy admits. Search: `grep -rn -i restrictive docs/adr packages/spec/src/security/rls.zod.ts` gives 2 ADR hits (ADR-0010, unrelated; ADR-0095 D1 delta (b), which is about the tenant wall) and 0 in the schema.

### Protocol statement

The protocol says a row policy admits rows, applicable policies add up, a row is denied only when no applicable policy admits it, and an update or delete policy means the same rows by id and in bulk. The member baseline is itself a shipped policy on `member_default`. The policy schema has no kind: its live keys are `name`, `label`, `description`, `object`, `operation`, `using`, `check`, `positions`, `enabled`.

- **A** changes no protocol (`Metadata-protocol: none`). It brings the by-id door back to the declared OR. Behaviour widens (`Clause-②: yes (widening)`).
- **B** adds no key, but it changes what an authored write `using` means: from "admits these rows" to "also caps what the shipped baseline policy admits, wherever record sharing vouches for the row". The spec's Default Deny sentence, the published skill text and two docs pages would have to carve the baseline out. That is the contract following one door's implementation.
- **C** is a protocol addition (`Metadata-protocol: added`, a new authorable key). By the dispatch rule a new public surface is its own card and is never a Bug option; it is listed so the ruling can say whether such a card should exist.

### Premises, each with a re-check

1. By id, a sharing `allow` deletes the baseline term. `sed -n '390,392p' packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-rls-filter.ts` reads `opts?.dropPlatformOwnershipFloor ? collected.filter((p) => !isPlatformOwnershipFloorPolicy(p)) : collected`.
2. In bulk, the baseline stays beside an authored term. `grep -n "if (replaced) return null" packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts` gives line 3053.
3. Main pins the disagreement. `grep -n "the by-id corner, reported out of scope" packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/predicate-write-floor-deferral.test.ts` gives line 531 (by id `.not.toContain('r1')`; line 527 has the bulk write changing `['r1', 'r2']`).
4. No restrictive kind exists. `grep -n -i -c restrictive packages/spec/src/security/rls.zod.ts` gives 0; the one `permissive` hit (:1084) is a helper's comment.
5. The baseline is a shipped, position-scoped policy. `grep -n -A5 "name: 'owner_only_writes'" packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/objects/default-permission-sets.ts` reads `object: '*'`, `operation: 'update'`, `using: 'created_by == current_user.id'`, `positions: ['org_member']`.
6. Real authors write wideners only. `grep -rn -A2 -E "operation: '(update|delete|all)' as const" /home/user/hotcrm/src --include=*.profile.ts | grep -E "using|check"` gives 2 hits at HotCRM `e7fe77f`, both `using: 'id != null'` (every row). `grep -rln rowLevelSecurity examples --include=*.ts | grep -v test` gives one file, the showcase, whose only write-class policy is check-only (`invoice_owner_immutable`). No example and no HotCRM rule is a cap written as `using`, and none is a partial widener.
7. ### The concrete question

When record sharing answers `allow` for a row, and an app-authored update or delete `using` policy applies to the caller but does not match the row, is a row the caller created admitted (the member baseline stays one OR term beside the authored policy, at both doors) or refused (the `allow` removes the baseline and the authored policy decides alone, at both doors)?

Not asked here: whether record sharing's `allow` should itself count as a term beside an authored policy. ADR-0066 ① answers no for Modify All on an ordinary object, and changing that is a protocol card.

### Options

| Option | What it does | What the customer sees | Effort |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| **A — admit** | By id, the baseline is dropped only where it is the last term; beside an authored `using` policy it stays one OR term (row gate, defaulted check, explain, master check). The bulk door already does this. The 22 fixtures are rewritten onto rows the delegator did not create. | The creator of a record can again edit and delete it one at a time when the rule does not match it, and bulk and single writes agree. An authored write rule no longer stops a record's creator; a cap on update is written as a check, a validation rule or a field lock, and a cap on delete as a hook. Owners who did not create the row, share holders and Modify All holders are held to the rule as today. | `domain:server` · 1 PR · built branch measured +314/−48 over 6 files (unlanded), plus the fixture rewrite in 2 test files (not written, not measured). Landed precedent in the family: #35914 +1064/−17, 6 files; #24792 +601/−20, 5 files. |
| **B — bound** | Today's by-id answer becomes the meaning. The bulk door is narrowed: every row record sharing allows drops the baseline even where an authored term remains. | Nobody a write rule applies to can write a row outside it once record sharing vouches for the row, the creator included. Flows and scheduled jobs that bulk-update or bulk-delete quietly write fewer rows than before (breaking). A builder who wants "owners, plus anyone on open deals" must restate ownership inside the rule. On objects with no owner field the creator still passes. | `domain:server` · 1 breaking PR · landed precedent: #35914 +1064/−17, 6 files, 13 commits (the last change to this bulk composition). It also re-scopes #35934. |
| **C — a restrictive kind** | Add an authorable kind so a widener ORs and a cap ANDs. Spec, compiler, explain, lint, docs, and an ADR. Not a Bug option. | Authors state "adds access" or "caps access" and get exactly that. Nothing changes until it ships; this card waits. | `domain:spec` + `domain:server` · ADR + at least 3 PRs · no precedent for a restrictive kind. Nearest landed protocol-key precedent: #24398 +549/−83, 26 files, with its lint follow-up #24511 +590/−133, 10 files. |

Considered and excluded: replacing the baseline with an always-true term (the card's literal "Expected" shape). It would let a Modify All holder write past any authored policy on an ordinary object, which ADR-0066 ① forbids and the card's own Done-when rules out. An option that conflicts with governing text is not a decision option.

### What each option means in business terms

- **A**: a rule that says "these people may also edit" never takes away what every member already has, the right to change what they created. Adding a rule only adds.
- **B**: once a builder writes one edit rule, that rule is the whole rulebook for the people it applies to, and ownership stops counting unless the rule says it again. One rule is a grant and a cap at once.
- **C**: two labelled drawers, grants and caps, as Postgres has PERMISSIVE and RESTRICTIVE policies.

### Four axes, from the business standpoint

**① Long-term soundness.** A builder needs one sentence for what a write rule does. The sentence the spec, the docs and the published skill already give is "a rule lets people change the rows it matches, and several rules add up". A keeps that sentence true at both doors and makes the hand-over from the member baseline to record sharing one-directional: it can add rows and never removes one. It also replaces two compositions held together by pins with one. B makes a single rule a grant in one place (it lifts a sharing refusal by id, by the #5493 ruling) and a cap in another (it removes what the baseline gave), depending on what record sharing answers for the row; on an object with no owner field the cap does not apply at all; and a bulk write needs a verdict per row to learn which reading holds. That is contract growth nobody declared. The platform has met this shape before: when the tenant boundary was found mis-modelled as an OR-able rule, it was given its own AND layer and OR kept its meaning (ADR-0095 D1). C is that same move for caps, and it is the mainstream shape, but it is a protocol card.

**② Real pull.** The only authors of write rules measured are HotCRM's marketing profile, with two rules, both "every row" grants written to add access, and the only pull that reached the maintainer in this family was for grants (#5492 and #5493, both from the HotCRM 17.0 acceptance sweep). The showcase writes its cap as a check, and the platform's own baseline set does the same. No customer has hit the disagreement: the dev rig found it, and HotCRM's rules match every row, so neither A nor B changes one HotCRM answer. Pull for a cap written as a write rule: zero.

**③ Keeping AI from getting it wrong.** Under A, an AI-authored app that tries to freeze records with a write rule gets no error: a record's creator keeps editing and deleting it. That is a silent over-admission, limited to rows the caller created and record sharing already lets them write; it never reaches another person's record. Under B, an AI-authored app that follows the taught sentence and adds a grant sees its owners refused on their own records one at a time (loud, fail-safe) and its bulk jobs quietly write fewer rows (silent). So B is louder at the single-record door, and A is the one under which the author who follows the contract as taught is right. The structural answer is C's closed two-value kind, where stating one and getting the other is impossible. Under A the misuse is met by the docs naming where a cap belongs, not by a new lint: new gates default to no.

**④ Startup focus.** A adds no key, no gate and no migration, and lands from a built branch. B is a breaking narrowing with a release note; it puts a per-row cost on every bulk write under any authored rule and re-opens a queued performance card. C is a permanent authorable key with an ADR, a compiler path, explain and lint behind it, for zero measured pull.

### Recommendation and confidence gaps

**Recommend A.** It is the only option under which both governing statements hold at once: applicable policies add up with no implicit deny (spec, ADR-0066 §3 and §4), and Modify All does not lift an authored write policy on an ordinary object (ADR-0066 ①). The by-id refusal is a side effect of #6684 that no ruling asked for, so this is code returning to the protocol. A is also the cheapest option; the recommendation does not rest on that.

- Not B: it bends the contract to one door's unruled side effect, breaks bulk callers silently, and leaves one rule acting as grant and cap.
- Not C: a new public surface with zero measured pull. If a customer asks for caps, it is a protocol card with its own ADR, not this Bug's fix.

Meta-criterion ② (one operation, two implementations: the governed side wins) reads toward B on its face. The by-id door is the one the bulk door was built to mirror, and it carries the per-row verdict, explain parity and the 22 pins. The criterion allows the reverse "only when product semantics clearly require it". I read the declared semantics above as requiring it. That reading is the maintainer's to confirm, and it is the reason this card is a decision and not a seat default.

Confidence gaps:

- The 22-red reading, and the claim that nothing else in the suite moves, are the dev's at `0f31476970`. I did not re-run the suite. Typecheck on the branch was not run by the dev either.
- A turns 22 pinned refusals on a p1 security card's fixtures into admissions. Those refusals date from #6684, not from before it, and D10 itself is untouched (the dev measured the direct and the delegated outcomes moving together). Whether each rewritten pin still goes red when the #24792 guard is removed is unverified; a pin that no longer discriminates must be reported, not kept green.
- An app that has relied since #6684 on a write rule stopping a record's creator by id would silently widen under A. None is measured, but only this repo's examples and one HotCRM checkout were read; the cloud app repo and live deployments were not.
- A leaves one asymmetry in place: under a partial widener, an owner who did not create the record is still refused on rows outside the rule, where without the rule record sharing admits them. Both doors agree on it and it predates #6684. Closing it means letting record sharing's `allow` stand beside authored policies, which is the excluded shape above and a protocol question.
- The card measured the engine door only; the REST door was not measured by anyone.

**End state.** In two years a write rule on ObjectStack has one meaning per kind: a row policy adds access beside record sharing and the member baseline, the way Postgres and Supabase PERMISSIVE policies add up and Salesforce sharing only ever opens access; a cap lives in its own declared home, today the write check, validation rules, stage-conditioned field locks and delete hooks (Salesforce's validation rules), and, once a customer pulls for it, an explicit restrictive kind as in Postgres `AS RESTRICTIVE`; and the same write gets the same answer one record at a time and in bulk.

**Self-check.** 「只看①选 A;②③④ 是否翻转:否」 (② and ④ read A; ③ reads mixed, louder under B at the single-record door, and does not turn the letter.)

### After the ruling

If A:

- Lane and PR: `domain:server`, the existing claim and branch `claude/issue-35917-by-id-widener-floor-term`, one PR. The claim is amended for one line outside its surface, the jsdoc of `RlsFilterOptions.dropPlatformOwnershipFloor` in `security-plugin.ts`, which must say the baseline is dropped only where it is the last term.
- The dev verifies first, on current main, before touching the fixtures: (1) the only reds in the full plugin-security suite are the 22 rows of the #24746 family; (2) every row whose answer changes is one the caller created and record sharing answers `allow` for; (3) `checkAuthoredRowWrite` still answers `abstain` for a row no authored policy matches, so the baseline never counts as an authored admission; (4) on every rewritten row the delegated outcome equals the delegator's own.
- Pins: the ones on the branch (owner-creator update and delete by id, the Modify All holder under the widener, the check control, the tenant wall, the owner-less control, by-id against bulk over the #35914 matrix, explain parity). The 22 rows are rewritten onto rows the delegator did not create and stay refused for both; a pair is added where the delegator created the held row and both the direct and the delegated write are admitted. Each pin is ablated, the rewritten ones against the #24792 guard as well.
- Owed before review: typecheck, and the three gate families the dev could not run on an unbuilt workspace.
- Declaration: `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, a `patch` changeset on `@objectstack/plugin-security`, naming the 22 refusals that become admissions. It is not breaking, so it carries no ADR-0087 disposition marker.
- Docs, inside the claim's surface: the sharing-rules line already on the branch, and one sentence in the RLS page saying a write rule adds rows and naming where a cap goes.
- Review: the contract-tier review the claim already owes, then L1.
- ⛔ Fork rule: if any of the four checks fails (a red outside the family, a changed answer on a row the caller did not create or record sharing does not allow, an authored admission earned by the baseline, or a delegated outcome that differs from the delegator's), the dev stops and reports a fork. ⛔ No partial landing, and no quiet fallback to B or to the always-true term.
- #35934: unblocked as written. Its case (iv), no verdict asked under an authored write policy, stays true and becomes exact parity with the by-id door; its equivalence matrix gains the widener rows. It still waits behind this PR on the shared files.

If B: the branch is dropped, #35917 closes as by design after a breaking bulk-door PR with the narrowing kit, and #35934 is re-scoped first because its case (iv) reverses. If C: an ADR card is filed and both #35917 and #35934 wait on it.
